_note: The status kubectl prints for a pod, in the one case both evaluators claim to answer: no init containers, no pod-level reason, no deletionTimestamp. Rust derives it for every live pod (src-tauri/src/resources/types/pod_display.rs); TypeScript derives it for a manifest somebody pasted into the infrastructure builder, where no cluster read happened (src/features/infrastructure/utils.ts). Two implementations in two languages, and this file is what holds them to the same answer. A case outside that subset — an init container blocking, a Completed pod with a live sidecar, a scheduling gate — belongs in the Rust tests alone; the TypeScript side does not claim it, and putting it here would only pin a disagreement.

cases.name: a container waiting for a reason names the pod
the first container's verdict is the one that stands
a running container leaves the phase standing
a terminated container names its reason
a terminated container with no reason names its exit code
a container killed by a signal names the signal
